question.text: Which of the following actions can a trader perform after placing an order in the derivatives segment?

answer.text: Modify the price, quantity, or cancel the order, provided it has not been fully executed
Modify orders even after full execution
Only cancel the order but cannot modify it
Modify the order type from limit to market after placement

explanation.text: The Logic: Pending (unexecuted or partially executed) orders sitting in the exchange order book can generally be modified or cancelled by the trader. The price can be changed, the pending quantity can be increased or reduced, or the order can be cancelled outright. Once an order is fully executed, however, no modifications are possible because the trade is already done. The Trap: Fully executed orders cannot be rewound or modified. Saying a trader can ONLY cancel and not modify is too restrictive, and saying the order type (limit, market, etc.) can be flipped after placement is typically not allowed - the usual practice is to cancel and re-enter rather than mutate the order type. Note: The cited pages of the NISM-Series-VIII Equity Derivatives workbook discuss order types and the cancellation of unexecuted Day/IOC orders and IRRA cancellation during service disruption, but do not explicitly describe a general post-placement modify capability for price and quantity. The framing above is general Indian exchange trading-system knowledge.
